answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to post a refundable stake that is slashed when peers prove fraud, turning cheap identity creation into a costly signal. Newcomers start with narrow permissions and only earn broader trust as verified work accumulates, so a flood of fresh accounts cannot outvote established ones at dawn of a market. Honest behavior is not a whisper lost in noise: attestations from independent, staked peers are weighted, making coordinated fake identities expensive to sustain while a single honest agent remains cheap to run.
